Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-05-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martin (Redwood AE), Sofia Perez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Cartwheel Head of Eng), Ravi Patel (Cartwheel Platform), Emily Chen (Cartwheel ML Eng)

Summary: Quick sync on the POC throughput optimization workstream. Reviewed last week's benchmark runs, discussed continuous batching and concurrency targets, surfaced queueing/backpressure behavior, and agreed on new 24h run and configuration changes (batch windows, target concurrency, grace queue size).

Topics: throughput numbers, continuous batching heuristics, concurrency vs latency tradeoff, KV cache / prefix caching, dedicated pool sizing, queueing/backpressure, next steps and owners.

Action items (auto-gen): see action_items metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, about 40 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Jordan here.
[00:09] Ravi Patel: Ravi here.
[00:10] Emily Chen: Emily on.
[00:11] Sofia Perez: Sofia, SE, I'm here.
[00:15] Alex Martin: Cool. Last week we ran the two hour burst test on the dedicated cluster, Sofia, can you recap the key numbers?
[00:23] Sofia Perez: Yeah, so recap, we had the dedicated pool with 8 GPUs, 16x batch workers, we pushed a synthetic pattern approximating peak shopping traffic. We saw aggregate throughput of ~750 tokens/sec per GPU for the 8 gpus, overall around 6k tokens/sec. Latency median stayed around 110ms per response but the tail (99th) spiked to 1.6s during surges. Also noticed a frequent small queue buildup when concurrency crossed 12 per worker.
[01:02] Ravi Patel: Is that 12 concurrency per worker or per GPU? I think our target was 16 per GPU.
[01:08] Sofia Perez: Sorry, that was per worker process; on our config each worker maps to 1/2 GPU so it maps to roughly 8 per GPU. The mapping got a bit confusing because of the container layout.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: Right, mapping matters. Our baseline goal is 120k tokens/minute for the homepage recommender API, which translates to about 2k tokens/sec sustained. We're clearly above that aggregate, but the tail spikes are painful for user experience.
[01:34] Alex Martin: Understood. The tradeoff we usually see is continuous batching increases throughput but can add latency for single-request flows unless you set concurrency targets & max batch windows carefully.
[01:45] Emily Chen: Can you remind us how Redwood's continuous batching triggers? Is it time-window based or adaptive by token length?
[01:52] Sofia Perez: It's hybrid — there's a short time window default (6-8ms) and an adaptive threshold that expands during low load. For long sequences we also use early-exec heuristics to not stall smaller requests. But in our test the short window plus the concurrency cap led to micro-queues.
[02:10] Ravi Patel: We also saw the KV cache hits drop during burst, I suspect cold cache on some sharded workers. The logs show some 'KV cash' errors — transcription note, actual log had KV cache misses — so the effective latency increased for those streams.
[02:27] Sofia Perez: Yeah, there was a bit of misalignment. We flagged a shard-placement issue, the cache warming didn't fully parallelize across the 8 gpus during the ramp. We've got a config tweak to change the cache prefetch concurrency.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: Ok. So what's the mitigation plan short-term? We can't afford 99th > 1s.
[02:44] Alex Martin: Short term we recommend two levers: lower max batch window from 8ms to 4ms for latency-sensitive routes, and raise the concurrency target per worker to absorb more in-flight requests without creating head-of-line blocking. But there's a sweet spot — too much concurrency increases memory and can degrade throughput due to context switching.
[03:05] Emily Chen: Did you try increasing the batching waterline rather than window? Like allow larger batch size but keep window small?
[03:12] Sofia Perez: We experimented — bigger batch size helps only if you can fill the batch quickly. In our bursty traffic we had intermittent micro-bursts and the bigger batch window just increased tail latency. So we prefer a smaller window + dynamic concurrency throttling.
[03:28] Ravi Patel: We noticed a pattern where after a surge, the queue length stayed high for a minute, not seconds. Could that be backpressure from downstream rate limiting?
[03:36] Sofia Perez: Possibly, or the de-queuing scheduler was in a degraded state due to GC pauses in the runtime. We saw a couple of pause spikes around 200-300ms in the runtime logs. We're going to dig into allocator settings.
[03:48] Alex Martin: For the POC next run, we suggested two benchmark profiles: 1) latency-sensitive: small requests, strict 99th < 300ms target; low batch window, concurrency 8 per GPU; 2) throughput-sensitive: fill batches, batch window 10ms, concurrency 16 per GPU, measure tokens/sec and cost. Cartwheel will run both.
[04:07] Jordan Lee: Makes sense. Any idea on cost delta if we go to the throughput-optimized config?
[04:12] Alex Martin: Rough estimate — throughput-optimized can improve tokens/sec per GPU by ~20-30% depending on model; that usually reduces unit cost but increases tail latency. We'll include a cost estimate in the config doc.
[04:22] Emily Chen: On model variants — we're testing the 7B quantized and the 13B int8. Which one was used in these runs?
[04:29] Sofia Perez: These tests were 13B int8. The 7B tends to have lower tail naturally but different quality tradeoffs. For throughput testing 13B is a good stress test.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: Can we try mixed routing — send 80% to 13B and 20% to 7B to lower load on the heavy model for tail-sensitive users?
[04:44] Alex Martin: Absolutely — smart routing is an option. In Redwood you can define route policies that fallback to smaller model when queueing exceeds threshold. We'll demo that in the deep-dive.
[04:53] Jordan Lee: About the queueing behavior — what's the 'grace queue' concept you mentioned earlier?
[04:58] Sofia Perez: Grace queue is a short FIFO buffer per worker that allows a tiny burst above concurrency target while tolerating a brief processing lag. It's like a leaky bucket. We can tune its size and max dwell time. In your runs, the grace queue default was 32 requests which led to long dwell times at 99th; we recommend reducing to 8 and couple with dynamic shed policy.
[05:18] Emily Chen: Dynamic shed meaning reject or route to fallback?
[05:21] Sofia Perez: Route to fallback model or region, or return fast-fail based on the policy. We prefer routing to fallback to keep user experience acceptable.
[05:28] Ravi Patel: Ok routing to fallback requires we setup the 7B in the same pool or at least reachable regionally. Is there an extra latency hit?
[05:35] Alex Martin: If it's same region and cold start not an issue, extra hop is minimal. But cross-region adds ~100-150ms sometimes. We'll factor that in.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: Let's talk numbers you want us to collect in the 24h run.
[05:48] Sofia Perez: Please collect: qps over time, tokens/sec, batch size distribution, per-worker concurrency histogram, 50/95/99/99.9 latency, KV cache hit rate, memory/GPU utilization, and any runtime pause events. Also include traces on a subset of requests for tail cases.
[06:06] Emily Chen: We can push logs to our S3-equivalent; what's the preferred format?
[06:10] Sofia Perez: CSV for metrics and JSONL for traces. We'll share the schema.
[06:15] Alex Martin: Good. On observability, we'll also enable the route-level tracing in the console so you can link traces to user ids (sanitized).
[06:23] Ravi Patel: One practical question — what should our concurrency target be for the next test? You suggested 16 earlier.
[06:29] Sofia Perez: For the throughput profile, set concurrency target to 16 per GPU. For latency profile, stick to 8 per GPU and batch window 4ms. We'll also add a middle profile with concurrency 12.
[06:40] Jordan Lee: Sounds fair. Any change needed to autoscaling? We saw slow scale-up when sustained qps rose.
[06:46] Alex Martin: For Dedicated you'll want more aggressive scale thresholds: lower the scale-out cooldown and increase provisioning burst size. That reduces the window where queuing grows while instances spin up. We'll send recommended autoscaler settings.
[06:59] Emily Chen: Are the scale-up times primarily infra boot or model warmup?
[07:04] Sofia Perez: Both. GPU nodes take time to spin, and model warmup depends on cache. We mitigate with warm standby and cold-start mitigation like prewarmed workers for critical routes.
[07:14] Ravi Patel: Prewarming sounds good but expensive. We'll evaluate cost.
[07:18] Alex Martin: Right, that's one of the levers — pay a bit more for prewarmed capacity to avoid tail spikes. We'll include cost delta in the doc.
[07:26] Jordan Lee: On security side, no change needed for these tests, right? We're using the dev VPC?
[07:31] Alex Martin: Correct dev VPC, logs remain within your bucket, no PII in traces unless you explicitly forward. We also have SOC2 docs already shared.
[07:40] Emily Chen: On the note about cache warming — can Redwood force a global prefetch across shards?
[07:46] Sofia Perez: We have a prefetch job that can warm the KV cache concurrently across GPUs; it's a config toggle. We'll share config and a sample prefetch job script.
[07:56] Ravi Patel: Prefetch typo noted.
[07:58] Sofia Perez: Yup, prefetch.
[08:00] Alex Martin: Quick check: does Cartwheel want Redwood to run the 24h test or will you run it?
[08:06] Jordan Lee: We prefer to run in our environment to capture full infra effects; Redwood can run a parallel run if helpful.
[08:13] Alex Martin: Ok we'll stand by and can run a controlled run in Redwood dedicated environment for apples-to-apples.
[08:19] Emily Chen: For the 24h run we'll start Friday 00:00 UTC to cover peak and off-peak. Is that OK?
[08:25] Alex Martin: Works. We'll coordinate.
[08:27] Sofia Perez: One more small bug: in the last run, the scheduler misreported batch sizes for a 10% of requests due to logging race. We'll patch and resend corrected metrics.
[08:38] Ravi Patel: Thanks.
[08:39] Jordan Lee: Anything else on tuning knobs?
[08:42] Sofia Perez: We'll provide a config template with: batch_window_ms, max_batch_size, concurrency_target, grace_queue_size, fallback_policy, cache_prefetch_concurrency, and runtime_allocator_flags.
[08:55] Emily Chen: Great. We'll use that template and post results.
[08:59] Alex Martin: Ok recap — next steps: Alex shares pricing + capacity doc, Sofia shares batching config + logs schema, Cartwheel runs 24h tests and shares artifacts. We'll meet same time next week to review.
[09:12] Jordan Lee: Confirmed.
[09:14] Ravi Patel: Confirmed.
[09:15] Emily Chen: Confirmed.
[09:16] Alex Martin: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[09:19] [call ends]
